q: 1. If the specific gravity and voids in soil sample are G and e respectively, the hydraulic gradient i, is
explain: The critical hydraulic gradient (at which quicksand condition occurs) is derived as icr = (G-1)/(1+e), balancing submerged weight against seepage force.

q: 2. During seepage through a soil, direction of seepage is always
explain: In a flow net, flow lines (direction of seepage) always cross equipotential lines at right angles, i.e., seepage is perpendicular to equipotential lines.

q: 3. The ultimate settlement of a soil is directly proportional to
options: depth of the compressible soil strata
explain: Consolidation settlement Sc = (Cc·H)/(1+e0)·log(...), directly proportional to both the thickness of compressible strata (H) and the compression index (Cc).

q: 4. The compression resulting from a long term static load and consequent escape of
explain: Consolidation is precisely the time-dependent compression caused by sustained static load driving pore water out of a saturated fine-grained soil.

q: 5. The reduction in volume of soil due to squeezing out of water from the voids, is termed
explain: The book lists all three terms (primary consolidation, primary compression, primary time effect) as synonymous descriptions of this volume-reduction phenomenon.

q: 6. The coefficient of permeability is proportional to void ratio as .............
explain: Permeability is commonly related to void ratio through the expression k ∝ e³/(1+e), based on Kozeny-Carman type relations.

q: 7. The permeability of the following soil will be almost zero .............
explain: Fine-grained content in silty/clayey sand fills the pore spaces, drastically reducing permeability compared to clean sands.

q: 8. The property of a soil which is of great importance in finding settlement of structures, is
explain: Consolidation behaviour (rate and magnitude of volume change under load) directly governs long-term settlement calculations for structures.

q: 9. Which of the following does not happen when compaction is done?
explain: Compaction is intended to increase soil density, which typically increases shear strength; therefore, a decrease in shear strength is what does NOT happen.

q: 10. The most effective method for compacting sand is by using .............
explain: Cohesionless sands compact best under vibratory compaction, which rearranges grains into a denser packing.

q: 11. Passive earth pressure is defined as
options: retaining wall tends to move away from the back fill
retaining wall tends to move towards the back fill
retaining wall is in stationary position
explain: Passive pressure develops when the wall is pushed into (moves towards) the backfill, compressing the soil to mobilize maximum resistance.

q: 12. Earth pressure at rest can be defined as lateral pressure exerted by the soil when the retaining wall tends to
options: no movement relative to the backfill
explain: At-rest earth pressure occurs when the wall is rigid and does not move at all relative to the backfill (zero lateral strain condition).

q: 13. The most suitable method for increasing the bearing capacity of black cotton soil is
options: replacement of black cotton soil by sand
explain: Because black cotton soil swells/shrinks excessively and has low bearing capacity, the most effective remedy is to replace it with a sand cushion/pad beneath the foundation.

q: 14. The consolidation settlement of a soil is
options: directly proportional to the voids ratio
explain: Consolidation settlement Sc = (Cc·H)/(1+e0)·log10[(σ0+Δσ)/σ0] is directly proportional to the compression index Cc.

q: 15. The value of net allowable bearing pressure is
options: minimum of net safe bearing capacity and net safe settlement pressure
explain: Net allowable bearing pressure is taken as the smaller (governing) value between the pressure limited by shear failure (net safe bearing capacity) and that limited by tolerable settlement.

q: 16. The Terzaghi's bearing capacity factors are functions of
options: friction angle between footing and soil
explain: Terzaghi's bearing capacity factors Nc, Nq, Nγ are all derived as functions solely of the soil's angle of internal friction φ.

q: 17. A flownet may be used for the determination of .............
explain: A flow net simultaneously provides exit gradient, seepage discharge, and seepage/uplift pressure at any point.

q: 18. Assumption in the Darcy' law is
explain: Darcy's law assumes an isotropic, homogeneous, incompressible, saturated soil with laminar (not turbulent) flow conditions.

q: 19. According to ISS the minimum depths of foundation in sand and clay should be respectively
explain: As per Indian Standard code recommendations, minimum foundation depth in sand and clay generally falls in the range of about 80 cm to 90 cm, considering seasonal moisture variation and frost/shrinkage effects.

q: 20. The maximum differential settlement is isolated footings on clayey soils should be limited to
explain: As per IS code guidance for isolated footings on clayey soils, the permissible differential settlement is typically limited to about 40 mm to avoid structural distress.

q: 21. Coefficient of percolation has a value .............
options: less than the coefficient of permeability
equal to the coefficient of permeability
explain: Percolation velocity uses the effective (void) area rather than the gross area, making the coefficient of percolation greater than the coefficient of permeability.

q: 22. The presence of entrapped air in a soil will .............
explain: Entrapped air bubbles block pore channels, reducing the effective flow path and thus decreasing permeability.

q: 23. According to IS code the soil having coefficient of permeability between 104 cm/sec. and 10-2 cm/sec. is termed as
explain: IS classification places soils with permeability in this intermediate range (between highly pervious and impervious) into the semi-pervious category.

q: 24. Coefficient of earth pressure at rest is
options: Less than active earth pressure but greater than passive earth pressure
Greater than active earth pressure but less than passive earth pressure
Greater than both the active earth pressure and passive earth pressure
Less than both the active and passive earth pressure
explain: Since Ka < K0 < Kp always (no wall movement gives an intermediate at-rest state between the minimum active and maximum passive states), K0 is greater than Ka but less than Kp.

q: 25. Capillary force is dependent on .............
explain: Capillary rise and force in soil pores are governed primarily by the surface tension of water acting at the air-water meniscus.

q: 26. Velocity head in soils will be .............
explain: Seepage velocities in soil are extremely small, making the velocity head component negligible compared to elevation and pressure heads.

q: 27. Water which the soil particles freely adsorb from atmosphere by the physical forces of attraction, and is held by the force of adhesion is known as .............
explain: Water adsorbed onto particle surfaces via physical attraction and adhesion can be described by any of these overlapping terms, so all apply.

q: 28. Units of co-efficient of permeability
explain: Coefficient of permeability k has units of velocity (length/time), commonly expressed as cm/sec, since it represents flow velocity under unit hydraulic gradient.

q: 29. Sheet piles are held in position by
options: Adjusting water level on one side
explain: Anchored sheet pile walls are stabilized primarily through tie rods connected to anchors set back in stable ground, in addition to embedment, but tie rods are the key holding mechanism cited here.

q: 30. Factor of safety of embankments shall be
explain: For slope stability of embankments against shear failure, a factor of safety of at least 2.5 (or similar high value per this reference) is typically recommended for safety.

q: 31. A critical hydraulic gradient occurs when .............
options: seepage pressure is in upward direction
explain: Critical gradient conditions require upward flow, upward seepage pressure equal to submerged weight, and consequently zero effective stress — all together.

q: 32. Geostatic stresses are due to .............
explain: Geostatic (overburden) stresses arise from the self-weight of the soil mass above a given point.

q: 33. Shearing strength of a cohesionless soil depends upon
explain: For a purely frictional cohesionless soil, shear strength (s = σ tanφ) is fundamentally governed by the normal stress on the failure plane.

q: 34. The law which states that the velocity of flow through porous medium is directly proportional to the hydraulic gradient is .............
explain: Darcy's law states that seepage velocity is directly proportional to hydraulic gradient, via v = Ki.

q: 35. Stability analysis shall be made considering .............
explain: Per the reference key this is marked 'shear stresses'; the widely accepted standard practice is that slope stability analysis should use effective stresses.

q: 36. The shear failure exhibited by loose sands is known as .............
explain: Loose sands compress and deform gradually under shear without a sharp peak, characteristic of plastic (ductile) failure.

q: 37. The height to which water can be lifted by capillarity is .............
options: independent of the atmospheric pressure value
depends upon the atmospheric pressure value
increases with decreasing diameter of the passage and is independent of the atmospheric pressure
explain: Per the reference key this is marked as depending on atmospheric pressure; the standard textbook fact is that capillary rise increases with decreasing pore diameter and is independent of atmospheric pressure.

q: 38. The ultimate strength of a loose and dense sand samples which are consolidated to the same value of effective stress will be .............
explain: At large strains (critical/ultimate state), both loose and dense sands consolidated to the same effective stress converge to the same ultimate strength.

q: 39. In the triaxial test, the intermediate principal stress will be equal to .............
options: average of major and minor principal stresses
explain: In a standard (axisymmetric) triaxial test, cell pressure acts equally on all lateral directions, so the intermediate principal stress equals the minor (confining) stress.

q: 40. The exit gradient of the seepage of water through a soil medium is the .............
options: ratio of total head to the length of seepage
ratio of the head loss to the length of seepage
explain: Exit gradient is defined as the head loss per unit length at the point where seepage exits the soil, i.e., head loss over seepage path length.

q: 41. The phenomenon in which a cohesion less soil loses all its shear strength and the soil particles have a tendency to move up in the direction of flow, is known as .............
explain: Boiling condition, quicksand, and quick condition are all terms used interchangeably for this loss of effective stress under upward seepage.

q: 42. Flow through an earth dam is a case of .............
explain: Seepage through an earth dam has a free (phreatic) surface exposed to atmospheric pressure, characterizing unconfined flow.

q: 43. The compression resulting from long term static load and resulting expulsion of water is known as .............
explain: Consolidation is precisely the gradual volume reduction from long-term static load causing pore water expulsion.

q: 44. Mathematically speaking, the time taken for 100% consolidation is .............
explain: Terzaghi's consolidation theory is an exponential/asymptotic process, so 100% consolidation is mathematically reached only at infinite time.

q: 45. The range of coefficient of permeability of sands is about .............
explain: Sands typically have permeability in the range of 10^-2 to 10^-4 cm/s, higher than silts and clays.

q: 46. Consolidation is generally considered to be a function of .............
explain: Consolidation behaviour (compression) is governed by changes in effective stress, per Terzaghi's principle.

q: 47. The unit of the coefficient of consolidation is .............
explain: Coefficient of consolidation Cv has units of area per time, i.e., cm2/sec.
